sentences: Because the boss believed the coworker could learn from their mistake, the chances for improvement were offered by the boss.
Because the truth was deliberately misrepresented by the employee, the coworker suffered unfair consequences.
Because the mistake was not prevented by the coworker, the responsibility was assigned by the boss.
Because the reputation was damaged by the employee's lie, the coworker experienced unjust harm.
